scientific_decision_snapshot.hypothesis: Does the current two-stage graph-memory core improve complete rolling-origin county forecasting over its matched no-memory control, and how does it compare with fixed practical baselines?
scientific_decision_snapshot.method: Hungarian Chickenpox,20physicalcounties,52pastweeks,313TRAIN/78VAL/79TEST targets. Generic mean-neighbor graph pass twice with shared weights, own-state residual,513parameter stable-entity memory, two directional GRUs and scalar external forecast. Full25378/NoMem24865parameters. Six full40epoch fits/4800updates, seeds101/202/303, matched initialization and batch order.
scientific_decision_snapshot.conclusion: All six 40-epoch fits, 4,800 updates and 15 TEST prediction products completed before scoring. On 79 TEST weeks and 20 counties, Full achieved MAE 13.907918 +/- 0.242561 and RMSE 24.268971 +/- 0.094496 cases. NoMem achieved 13.648097 +/- 0.050932 and 24.408159 +/- 0.106380, with sample SD across three initialization seeds. Both outperform the three frozen practical controls. Full failed the registered memory criterion: MAE was 1.904% worse, with paired difference +0.259820 cases and conditional 95% interval [+0.105412, +0.427353] using 13-week blocks. RMSE improved. This negative result is retained without retuning or replay. It is neither ancestry accuracy nor population generalization.
